answer: No. Under Condition 11 (Events of Default) of the Terms and Conditions, a failure to pay principal or interest does not give Noteholders a right to declare their Notes immediately repayable. If such a payment default continues for 30 days or more after the due date, the only remedy is that any holder may institute proceedings for the dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer in Belgium. The acceleration right arises only in the event of a dissolution or liquidation of the Issuer (including bankruptcy (faillissement/faillite), judicial liquidation or voluntary liquidation, other than a voluntary liquidation in connection with a reconstruction, merger or amalgamation where the continuing corporation assumes all liabilities of the Issuer) under Belgian law: each holder may then give written notice to the Paying Agent that its Notes are immediately repayable, whereupon the Event of Default Redemption Amount plus accrued interest becomes immediately due and payable. Resolution action by the Relevant Resolution Authority or suspension of payment obligations does not entitle holders to accelerate, and no other remedy is available. The risk factors confirm investors have no right of acceleration upon a payment default.
